speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to begin my assessment, how long has this dizziness been lasting, and is it constant or does it come in episodes? Additionally, do you experience any nausea, vomiting, or hearing changes alongside the vertigo?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The patient is a 59-year-old male presenting with sudden-onset vertigo lasting approximately 3 minutes, accompanied by nausea and vomiting, which resolved to baseline. The brief, episodic nature of the spinning sensation is highly characteristic of BPPV. Given the classic presentation, I will now request the Dix-Hallpike test results to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Dix_Hallpike
